newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Mobil sues Australian construction unions.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Mobil sues Australian construction unions.

text.p: Mobil Corp's Australian unit said on Thursday it was seeking an injunction to stop union industrial action which was delaying construction of a A$250 million fluidised catalytic cracker (FCC) at its Altona refinery in Victoria.

"We are disappointed that we have been forced to take this action, but we have been left with no alternative. Repeated attempts to negotiate with the unions have been unsuccessful," Mobil project manager Russell Gillespie said in a statement.

Mobil said the three unions involved had ignored a January 20 Australian Industrial Relations Commission (AIRC) order to cease industrial action at the site of the 24,000 barrel per day (bpd) FCC which was currently six months behind schedule.
Mobil spokeswoman Samantha Potts told Reuters the FCC would not be commissioned until mid 1997 at the earliest.

Mobil said it was mounting the legal action in conjunction with the FCC project manager, Japan's Toyo Engineering Corp, in the Federal Industrial Relation Court which will hear the matter on Tuesday, February 4.
Toyo and Mobil decided to hire new contractors for the FCC project in November last year after terminating the construction contract with John Holland Group over delays.
However, unions were agitating to have workers that would have been used by John Holland re-employed for the FCC job and were "persuading" the new workers not to start, Potts said.
"The (new) contractors are telling us they are prepared to work but their employees aren't prepared to start work because of the industrial action by the unions," she said.
A union spokesperson was not immediately available for comment.

Potts declined to comment on the cost of the delays. In July, Mobil said it would lose A$2 million for each week the commissioning of the new cracker was delayed beyond its original January 1 start date.
The FCC will eventually replace a thermal catalytic cracker of similar capacity at the refinery.
The FCC dispute was not affecting production or maintenance at the rest of the refinery, which was operating at 116,000 bpd, Mobil's Potts said.
